market_summary: The completed US equity session is constructive but selective, based on 1864 articles from Yahoo Finance, marketbeat.com, simplywall.st, TradingView, moomoo.com. The dominant theme is macro, with 910 macro items, 533 company items, 369 industry items, and 52 policy items. The tape looks more useful for identifying near-term rotation and risk appetite than for making a single directional index call.
market_narrative: US equities have a constructive but selective bias as Fed/rates, inflation, oil/energy dominate the information flow. The close should be judged by index breadth, Treasury yields and whether leadership broadened beyond the largest stocks.
index_performance_summary: Nasdaq and growth indexes should be the most sensitive part of the tape when AI, semiconductor, mega-cap tech, or guidance stories dominate. S&P 500 direction is likely to remain tied to Treasury yields, Fed expectations, inflation data, and broad risk appetite. Dow and equal-weight exposure may react more to policy, regulation, tariff, and industrial-cycle headlines.
macro_outlook: Macro coverage is concentrated around Fed/rates (289), inflation (263), oil/energy (160), growth/jobs (27). The practical implication is that equity rallies may need confirmation from rates and inflation expectations; if yields rise while growth headlines weaken, risk appetite can fade quickly.
risk_and_sentiment: Sentiment is constructive but selective: 341 positive, 163 negative, and 1360 neutral articles. My read is to avoid treating headline volume as conviction by itself; the more important signal is whether macro-sensitive and technology-sensitive stories are pointing in the same direction.
